stories.title: Man, 21, dies following assault in Dublin city centre
stories.summary: An investigation is under way after a 21-year-old man died following an assault in Dublin city centre in the early hours of this morning. The man was found on Clarendon Street, which is located close to Grafton Street, in a serious condition at around 3am. He was taken to St James's Hospital, where he was pronounced dead a short time later. Several scenes around Grafton Street have been preserved for forensic examination and the Office of the State Pathologist has been informed.

stories.title: Law removing Triple Lock expected to pass by year end
stories.summary: Legislation to remove the Triple Lock is expected to be enacted by the end of the year. Minister for Defence Helen McEntee is expected to bring the Defence (Amendment) Bill 2026 to the Cabinet for approval in the coming weeks. The bill removes the requirement for UN approval when deploying members of the Defence Forces outside the State. Last week, Ms McEntee told Cabinet colleagues that the importance of the legislation was underscored by Ireland's recent withdrawal from Operation IRINI - a European anti-arms smuggling naval mission in the Mediterranean - because the UN Security Council's mandate for the mission had lapsed.

stories.title: Two further arrests after PSNI officer injured in Co Down
stories.summary: A 36-year-old man and a 27-year-old woman have been arrested following an incident in which a PSNI officer was injured. The officer was struck by a stolen police vehicle in Co Down in the early hours of yesterday morning. A police spokesperson said a vehicle failed to stop for police in the Fountain Street area of Downpatrick at around 4.45am and was later located in the Ballymote Walk area. Police officers saw a man get out of the vehicle and "a foot pursuit ensued towards the Colmcille Road".

stories.title: 'It all works out,' Everest climber tells LC students
stories.summary: The youngest Irish person to summit Mount Everest has shared his advice to students who are about to sit their Leaving Cert exams. Adam Sweeney, 22, from Dunmore East, Co Waterford wants pupils who may be nervous or worried about their exams to know that "it all works out the way it's meant to work out". "I suppose, for the Leaving Cert, it probably does feel like an Everest, but then in five years' time, you’ll look back and almost forget what results you got," he said. "You think everything comes down to this in life, but you’ll get through it so quickly."

stories.title: UK govt braced for massive release of Mandelson files
stories.summary: The British government is braced for further embarrassment as hundreds of documents covering Peter Mandelson’s appointment and activities as ambassador to the US are expected to be published this afternoon. The massive release of files is the second relating to Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s decision to give the prestigious Washington job to Mr Mandelson rather than a career diplomat. Cabinet minister James Murray said there would be an "unprecedented" volume of information given to parliament. Officials have compared the scale of the effort examining documents related to Mr Mandelson to the sifting and disclosure of information to the UK Covid-19 Inquiry.
